- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 2–3 periods.  
- If model shows strong mean reversion bias (e.g., forecasting downward from high prices), check if sentiment is neutral or negative — if so, allow for a 1–2% upward correction to avoid overcorrection.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; if sentiment shifts sharply within 5–7 days, adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change within 1–2 periods.  
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.5–0.67), model tends to average out — avoid overfitting to recent history; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% sentiment).
